anchors: a one-slot cache keyed by object identity removes the repeats with bounded memory
decision: Repeated decoding of one immutable, unhashable parsed node is removed with a one-slot identity cache stored as one tuple, valid only when the result depends on the node alone and the node is frozen all the way down.

evidence.text: A one-slot cache on a decoded module cut export CPU from 23.9-24.6 s to 21.3-21.6 s interleaved and pinned, byte-identical output, mutation-tested.

reopen_if: A measurement shows the identity check missing repeats (readers receive equal but distinct nodes).
why: It avoids hashing the tree, keeps memory bounded, and a single tuple keeps a free-threaded reader from pairing one node with another's result.

decision: A compiled regex whose match can start at many positions of one run and then read to the run's end is quadratic under finditer/search/sub/findall; the two named shapes (CLASS+ before a required suffix, and a newline start alternative followed by \s*) are fixed with a same-class negative lookbehind and with [^\S\n]* after the anchor, proved by a growth-ratio test (one run per character kind) plus an old/new replay over real inputs comparing what the caller uses. It is filed as Unsafe Input: SEVERE when the scanned text can grow without bound or real input already costs seconds per run, MEDIUM when it only costs measurably on a hot path.

evidence.text: Shape 1: 3.47 ms at 2,000 chars and 222.8 ms at 16,000 (64.3x) against 0.022 and 0.162 ms anchored (7.5x), identical spans on 7 samples. Shape 2: 0.42 ms at 500 blank lines and 25.7 ms at 4,000 (60.5x) against 7.9x with [^\S\n]*; spans move on inputs with blank lines before the command, verdicts equal. A narrower lookbehind (?<![\w]) stays 61x on a './' run; a wider one drops 'b.py' after '+'.

reopen_if: find_uncompiled_regex.py or another bundled scanner flags these shapes itself, so the prose can point at it instead.
why: Both shapes shipped in hooks and passed three review rounds; neither short inputs, a normal-data profile nor find_uncompiled_regex.py shows them. One rule with both shapes as examples keeps the cause in one place.

decision: find_uncompiled_regex.py names four quadratic-start shapes: the two of d-20261119-a189b19d plus group-run-before-suffix (a repeated group such as (?:[\w.-]+/)+ before a required suffix; fix with a lookbehind of every character the run holds, or one fixed piece before the suffix when the caller needs only the verdict) and repeat-after-optional-prefix (a repeat reached past an optional prefix, every unit of its run a start; keep the body from crossing what the anchor needs). A class run behind an optional prefix keeps the class shape. The report opens with an 'Examined S regex call sites in F files' line counting checked, not-modelled and run-time-built patterns; the unchecked ones go to hand review, and S = 0 exits 2 with 'ERROR examined 0 regex call sites'.
